GDP Growth (%)': [2.15, 1.9, 0.5, 4.9, 2.95, 2.1, 3.4, 3.7, 6.5, 1.8] } df = pd.DataFrame(data) df_melted = df.melt(id_vars=['Country', 'Avg. Urban Growth (%)', 'Avg. GDP Growth (%)'], value_vars=['2018', '2019', '2020', '2021'], var_name='Year', value_name='Migrant Inflows (k)') pivot_df = df_melted.pivot_table(index='Country', columns='Year', values='Migrant Inflows (k)') fig = px.imshow( pivot_df, labels=dict(x="Year", y="Country", color="Migrant Inflows (thousands)"), color_continuous_scale='Viridis', aspect="auto" ) fig.update_layout( title='Annual Migrant Inflows Across Southeast Asian Countries (2018-2021)', title_x=0.5, width=900, height=700, margin=dict(l=100, r=50, t=80, b=100), xaxis_title='Year', yaxis_title='Migrant Inflows (thousands)', coloraxis_colorbar=dict( title='Migrant Inflows
(thousands)', tickvals=[50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300] ) ) fig.write_image('output.png') SUMMARY This chart is a heatmap that illustrates the annual migrant inflows across various Southeast Asian countries from 2018 to 2021. The heatmap uses a color gradient to represent the volume of migrant inflows, with the scale ranging from dark purple to bright yellow, indicating lower to higher values, respectively. The vertical axis lists the countries: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia, and Brunei, while the horizontal axis represents the years from 2018 to 2021. In the heatmap, Malaysia consistently shows the highest migrant inflows, with values peaking at 285,000 in 2019, represented by the brightest yellow shade. The inflows slightly decrease to 260,000 in 2020 but rise again to 275,000 in 2021. Thailand follows as the country with the second-highest inflows, with figures around 225,000 in 2018, reaching up to 240,000 in 2019, and experiencing a dip to 215,000 in 2020 before climbing back to 230,000 in 2021. Singapore also displays relatively high migrant inflows, ranging between 130,000 and 158,000 throughout these years. Vietnam, Indonesia, and the Philippines exhibit moderate migrant inflows, with Vietnam ranging from 52,000 to 58,000, Indonesia from 75,000 to 85,000, and the Philippines from 95,000 to 105,000. Laos, Myanmar, and Cambodia have lower inflows, with Laos peaking at 26,000 in 2019 and Myanmar and Cambodia showing figures mostly below 50,000. Brunei consistently has the lowest migrant inflows, never exceeding 6,000 in any given year. The color intensity in the heatmap effectively highlights these variations, providing a clear visual representation of the migrant inflow trends across the specified countries and years. source = Path("chart.py").read_text()
assert "yaxis_title='Migrant Inflows (thousands)'" in source
source = source.replace("yaxis_title='Migrant Inflows (thousands)'", "yaxis_title='Country'")
Path("chart.py").write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))
print("Y-axis title:", fig.layout.yaxis.title.text)
print("X-axis title:", fig.layout.xaxis.title.text)
print("Chart title:", fig.layout.title.text)
print("Color scale:", fig.layout.coloraxis.colorscale)
expected = pd.read_csv("table.csv").set_index("Country")
actual = pivot_df.loc[expected.index, expected.columns]
assert (actual.to_numpy() == expected.to_numpy()).all()
assert fig.layout.yaxis.title.text == "Country"
print("All heatmap values match table.csv.")
